posts.caption:
Your friend sends their bad news, and you text back "have sabr". That word asks them to hold on to themselves.

In Surah al-Kahf (18:28), Allah tells the Prophet, peace be upon him, "keep yourself patient" with the people who call on their Lord morning and evening. Ibn Faris's classical dictionary files sabr under holding something back. So on your own bad week, it means holding yourself back from what you'd regret, and holding yourself to what you still have to do. In 2:153, Allah puts it right next to prayer.

So next time, send your friend one more line: "Hold on to yourself, and keep praying. I'm making du'a for you."

Send this to the friend you said it to.

Word meanings: Quran Foundation. Translation: Saheeh International (QuranEnc.com).

Maana teaches the Qur'an's most common words. Pre-order on the App Store.

#sabr #patience #quranicarabic #quranwords #learnquran

gates.label: Sounds like a person talking to you

advisory.why: The hook has me texting a friend. Slides 3 and 4 turn to my own bad week, then slides 5 and 6 go back to the friend. I follow it, but I feel the swing.

gates.label: Correctness (Sunni sources)

advisory.why: Ibn Faris's example is the first-person "صبرت نفسي على ذلك الأمر" (I held myself to that matter). "A man" and "a task" are a loose paraphrase. It is not wrong, but "holding himself to a matter" or "I held myself to that matter" is closer.
advisory.fix: Reword to "his example is someone holding themselves to a matter".

needs_reviewer.quote: wa-ṣbir is the command form of the verb
needs_reviewer.why: Confirm the Arabic grammar term and the transliteration "wa-ṣbir" with maana-arabic-expert (QPC 18:28 word 1, وَٱصۡبِرۡ).

before_posting: Confirm the rendered slide 5 shows "Translation: Saheeh International (QuranEnc.com)" under the ayah and that the ayah image comes from quran_layer.py with 2:153 shown.

gates.label: Islamic correctness

advisory.why: This is the writer's own illustration of "holding yourself to what you must do". It is not in any card, and it can read as a mild guilt nudge for a viewer who is already struggling and missing Fajr. It does not state a ruling.
advisory.fix: Use a neutral example such as "holding yourself to the prayer you still have to make", or soften it to "even a short prayer".

needs_reviewer.quote: hold yourself back from what you'd regret ... hold yourself to what you still have to do
needs_reviewer.why: The Sunni sources (Raghib, Baghawi on 18:28, Tabari on 2:45) support sabr as holding the self. Please confirm that the applied examples (the angry reply, Fajr, "keep praying") are fine as the brand's own illustration and not attributed to a source.

before_posting: Check that the 2:153 ayah image shows the surah:ayah reference and the Saheeh International (QuranEnc.com) credit under it, and that only word 5 (بِٱلصَّبْرِ) is highlighted.
Check that the caption credits "Quran Foundation" and the translation line, and that the Pre-order line matches the launch state in decisions.json.
Confirm the "910 words" and "learned words light up green" lines against the live rows in facts.md (the post lists word-deck and words-light-up).
